title: openai-responses-compat: add seed/determinism + metadata passthrough + streaming stability fixes
author: Maya Patel
description:
Context: The OpenAI Responses API rollout includes variant response formats and explicit seed/determinism controls. Several customers and internal evaluators reported mismatches between Redwood's OpenAI-compat layer and vendor responses: (1) seed (randomness) parameter was being ignored for deterministic evaluation runs, (2) metadata passed in the Responses 'metadata' object was dropped at the compatibility layer, and (3) streaming mode could hang when downstream tooling/function-calling handshake had trailing empty chunks. Motivation: Fix compatibility regressions so Redwood can be used as a drop-in replacement for downstream test harnesses, and improve streaming reliability for function/tool-calling workloads.

Summary of changes (single-line commit summary list): commit 1: compat: respect "seed" and determinism flags in responses adapter; commit 2: passthrough: preserve top-level metadata fields from Responses schema into Redwood request context and logs; commit 3: streaming: add backpressure/timeouts for trailing-empty-chunk edgecases and ensure function-calling handshake finishes; commit 4: tests: add unit/integration tests for seed determinism and metadata propagation; commit 5: docs: update openai-compat/README and changelog.

Files changed (high level): src/openai_compat/responses_adapter.py - core adapter logic (seed/determinism handling); src/streaming/connection.py - streaming handshake/backpressure; src/streaming/tests/test_streaming_tool_call.py - new flaky-case test; src/openai_compat/tests/test_seed_and_metadata.py - determinism tests; docs/openai-compat.md - updated examples; examples/responses/seed-and-metadata.py - example usage; rust-runtime/src/kv_cache.rs - small tweak to preserve metadata in logs; ci/workflows/compat-tests.yaml - added nightly compat matrix.

Why this approach: Keeping the seed/determinism flag handling centralized in responses_adapter.py avoids duplicating logic across model runners; we map OpenAI's "temperature=0 + seed=X" pattern into Redwood's deterministic sampling when the runtime supports a seed, otherwise emulate deterministic outputs for tests by seeding sampler. For metadata passthrough we add a small opaque metadata bag to the request context and thread it through the common tracing/logging pipeline so it shows up in request-level logs and can be surfaced in Console and audits without changing core model inputs.

Testing notes and CI behavior: Local unit tests added for determinism check (seed value produces repeatable token sequences under the seedable runner). Integration tests run against a small deterministic model in the perf-canary infra; initial CI runs showed an intermittent streaming e2e failure (timeout waiting for function-calling "end_of_call" sentinel). I added a 200ms jitter-tolerant timeout and a more explicit end-of-stream sentinel, which stabilized the test. CI summary: unit-tests: pass; integration-tests: pass (after rerun); lint: pass; e2e/streaming: flaky on first run -> rerun -> pass. Release notes and changelog updated.
diff_snippets:
+    if 'seed' in responses_payload:
+        request_context.seed = int(responses_payload['seed'])
+        sampler.seed(request_context.seed)

-    # previously dropped metadata
+    request_context.metadata = responses_payload.get('metadata', {})
+    trace.log('responses.metadata', request_context.metadata)

+    # ensure streaming handshake completes even with trailing empty chunks
+    while not handshake.completed:
+        await asyncio.wait_for(handshake.next_chunk(), timeout=0.2)

+    # opt-in redact list to avoid logging PII
+    if key in redact_list:
+        safe_log(key, '[REDACTED]')
release_notes: Compatibility: Responses API: respect seed/determinism flags and passthrough top-level metadata; Stability: streaming handshake/backpressure fixes for function/tool-calling; Docs: examples and openai-compat README updated; No breaking changes.
review_comments: Ethan Park: Can we make seed a noop on non-seedable runners? If not, we should document behavior.
Maya Patel: Implemented a sampler-based emulation and added tests (src/openai_compat/tests/test_seed_and_metadata.py).
Lena Ortiz: Don't log metadata by default — privacy concerns. Added opt-in redact list and docs notes.
Samir Kaur: Found a race during connection teardown. Fixed in connection supervisor and added backoff; re-ran e2e and it's stable.
notes: Backported small runtime log change to rust-runtime for auditability. This PR was kept intentionally narrow to reduce blast radius; follow-up planned to support seed propagation end-to-end for non-deterministic sharded runners (ENG-3340).
security_implications: metadata passthrough is opt-in for console/audit surfaces; added redact-list to avoid accidental PII logging
